newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy premier Prodi says ERM re-entry step to EMU.
newsitem.headline: Italy premier Prodi says ERM re-entry step to EMU.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said the lira's re-entry into the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) was a "fundamental step" towards joining European economic and monetary union in 1999, Italian news agency ANSA reported.
"This result represents a premise for the lowering of the cost of money and constitutes a fundamental step for our participation in monetary union," the news agency quoted Prodi as saying.
"To have brought the lira into Europe is the consequence of the seriousness of our economic policy and of the stability we have given the country," Prodi said.
Italy has said repeatedly it sees bringing the lira back into the ERM as enhancing its chances of joining an advanced party of EU countries in the launch of a single currency in 1999.
